text:
zoe: hi folks, new here. VPN (Okta AnyConnect via openconnect) connects but short hostnames like `db1` or `build` don't resolve to the internal zone. FQDNs like `db1.internal.redwood.dev` work. On Fedora 37 with NetworkManager + systemd-resolved. any ideas?
kevin: welcome! sounds like search domain / DNS suffix isn't being pushed into your resolver. `resolvectl status` or `systemd-resolve --status` should show per-link domains.
zoe: `resolvectl status` shows the VPN link has "Domains: " but my default link has search for my wifi. Looks like systemd prefers the wifi link for short name lookups.
maria: yep this is a systemd-resolved quirk with split-tunnel. Two quick workarounds: (A) add the internal search domain to your main connection (NetworkManager GUI / nmcli) so short names resolve, (B) use the FQDN everywhere (more work), or (C) add `127.0.0.53 db1` entries in /etc/hosts (temporary).
kevin: to add via nmcli: `nmcli connection modify "Wired connection 1" ipv4.dns-search "internal.redwood.dev"` then `nmcli connection up <name>`. Alternatively `sudo resolvectl domain <ifindex> ~internal.redwood.dev` will set it for the VPN link (til reboot).
zoe: i'd prefer an automated approach. is there a managed policy for this? i don't want to manually change connections on a company laptop.
maria: infra can push a NetworkManager dispatcher script that adds the DNS search when the VPN interface comes up for managed machines. open an infra ticket and reference this thread. For personal machines we recommend the nmcli approach or using FQDNs.
infra-bot: Docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/vpn/systemd-resolved-searchdomains  includes nmcli samples and a dispatcher script snippet. Ticket template: https://infra.redwood.internal/tickets/new (select "VPN split-tunnel: DNS search domain").
zoe: thanks everyone  setting the dns-search on my connection fixed short names. i'll open a ticket for managed-policy. will also add a short note to my onboarding checklist. :+1:
